title: Concurrency is not parallelism: what Go actually promises

videos.script: This course is about the part of Go that most languages bolt on afterwards. Running many things at once, with nothing but the standard library. {{lab}} First, your machine. It is the one the go course built, with one addition. The race detector needs a C compiler, so you install gcc, and then four commands prove everything answers. {{spin}} Then two words people use as one. Concurrency is how a program is written: four independent tasks. Parallelism is how one run goes: how many of them execute at the same instant. You run the same program on one processor and on four, and watch the time fall from one and a half seconds to under half of one. {{wait}} Next, four tasks that only wait. On one processor they still finish in one second, not four. {{race}} Last, what Go promises. Not the order goroutines run in. It promises what happens when they synchronise, and it gives you a tool that catches them when they do not. {{close}} Lesson 2 shows what a goroutine actually costs.
